title: Reorder List
prompt:
Reorder the list `L0 → L1 → … → Ln` into `L0 → Ln → L1 → Ln-1 → L2 → …`, in place (rearrange nodes; don't change values).

**Example**: `[1,2,3,4,5]` → `[1,5,2,4,3]`.

All three linked-list moves composed: (1) fast/slow to find the middle, (2) reverse the second half, (3) merge the two halves alternately.
hints: Step 1: fast/slow — slow lands on the middle; cut with `second = slow.next; slow.next = null;`
Step 2: reverse `second` with the standard four-liner.
Step 3: alternate-splice — save both `next`s first, then rewire, then advance.

solution.explanation: O(n)/O(1). Note the middle-finder uses `fast.next != null && fast.next.next != null` so slow stops at the END of the first half (for even lengths), making the first half never shorter than the second — which the merge loop relies on.
